title: wikiskill task suite
description: A declarative set of evaluation tasks: prompts, expected routes, verifiers, rubric references, splits, fixtures and required capabilities. Tasks are data, so adding one changes no shared code.

suite.description: Suite id. Reported with every result, so it has to survive being put in a filename.

defaults.description: Applied to any task that does not set them itself.

split.description: Which split a task belongs to: train for refinement, val for tuning, test held out. Recorded with every result; review, refine and replay do not yet filter by it.

requires.description: Capabilities the run environment must provide. An unmet requirement skips the task with a reason; it is never scored as a failure. A task's list, empty included, replaces the suite default's; `requires: []` requires nothing.

setup.description: Shell commands run in the workdir, in order, after fixtures are copied and before the session starts. A failing command makes the unit an infrastructure error, never a model failure. A task's list, empty included, replaces the suite default's; `setup: []` runs no commands.

env.description: Environment variables set in each unit's harness process. A task's values override the suite defaults'. Names the runner uses for isolation are refused.

secrets.description: Names of host environment variables that only the declaring task's command verifiers receive. The runner removes every secret the suite declares from every task's session, any export step, setup commands and the `requires` check. A task's list is joined with the suite default's, unlike `requires`, `setup` and `guard`, which a task replaces; `secrets: []` withholds nothing less. A name any task's `env` sets or expands, or one the runner uses for isolation, is refused. This keeps the value out of the session environment and the records, not out of reach of an agent running as the same user, which can read the user's files and /proc/<pid>/environ.

guard.description: Command patterns the guard plugin blocks for this task, on top of the runner's own deny-by-default permissions. A task's guard, empty included, replaces the suite default's; `guard: {}` denies no patterns.

route.description: The route a correct run takes: which component should be activated, and which agents it should reach.

verifier.description: A deterministic check run in the task's workdir after the session. Verifiers decide pass or fail; a rubric judge only scores its own dimensions.

run.description: command: the shell command to run in the workdir.

result.description: command: `json` reads stdout as one JSON object (or its last non-empty line as one) and keeps it with the unit's verifier record. Output that is not a JSON object is an infrastructure error.

pass_when.description: command, with `result: json`: top-level result fields and the values each may hold. The verifier passes when the exit code matches `expect_exit` and every field holds one of its values.

score.description: command, with `result: json`: a top-level numeric result field that reports average per task, model and condition, beside the pass rate.

path.description: file_exists: a path relative to the workdir. Absolute paths are rejected.

target.description: regex: what the pattern is matched against.

negate.description: Pass when the check does NOT hold.

id.description: Unique within the suite, and usable as a directory name.

prompt.description: The user turn the model sees. It must not name the skill, agent or plugin it is expected to route to.

rubric.description: Path to a rubric file, relative to the suite file.

fixtures.description: Directory copied into the run's workdir, relative to the suite file.

followups.description: Scripted user turns to send after the first response. Not a simulated user. Accepted but not yet sent: no evaluation backend sends them, so the task runs on its first prompt only, and `suite check` warns.
